source: the wowsims/forever EP presets for a Holy priest (the mean of 'Holy Raid Healing' and 'Holy Single-Target', tools/data/ep_presets.json), applied to every healer spec; community EP weights, not a ForeverSim run, so the line is marked approximate
model: weighted score = 1 * +Healing, 1 * Spell Power, 0.325 * Intellect, 0.275 * Spirit, 0.6 * MP5, 0.265 * Crit and 0.49 * Haste
note: ForeverSim does not simulate healing, so no measured stat weights exist for a healer. This one model rates every healer spec (druid Restoration, priest Holy, paladin Holy, shaman Restoration) with the same weights: the sim repo's own EP presets for a Holy priest (Healing 1, Crit 0.265, Haste 0.49, Intellect 0.325, Spirit 0.275, MP5 0.6, the mean of its raid-healing and single-target presets). They replace an earlier hand-chosen guess (Intellect 0.5, Spirit 0.5, MP5 2, no Crit or Haste), which overvalued MP5 three to ten times against these presets. Assumptions: (1) a point of Spell Power (ITEM_MOD_SPELL_POWER_SHORT) is the same bonus as a point of +Healing (ITEM_MOD_SPELL_HEALING_DONE_SHORT), and an item the client reports with both keys is counted through both; (2) the weights are those of a priest and are used for the other healers as they are (a paladin or a shaman may want more Crit or Intellect); (3) spell ranks, talents, procs, overheal and cast uptime are not modelled. The percentage shown is the change in this score against the equipped item: an approximate healer ITEM score, not an actual healing increase. Generated into Weights.lua by tools/make_weights.py.
